status: Form-specific source checks, internal editorial review, content/dictionary/audio/browser/build and production offline gates passed; native review pending.
method: Original vocabulary examples, two conversations and two essays. Read teacher and grammar-publisher explanations; no source example, textbook passage, test item or recording is imported. Publisher level tags are editorial, not official JLPT certification.

points.formation: Noun/na-adjective stem + である, negative ではない, past であった. Verbs/i-adjectives retain their own plain conjugations.
points.teachingChoice: Written-style bridge: the selected publisher tags である N3. N2 unit 1 applies it to original essays rather than claiming it is newly N2-exclusive. Conversation stays casual or ordinary polite; a quoted draft uses formal writing.
points.sourceCaution: The complete guide's formal-writing section was readable. Its standalone formal page timed out; that page is not counted as inspected. A written copula is neither keigo nor a marker that a statement is proven.

points.form: Verb stem and であり connecting written clauses
points.formation: Use the ます-stem for a continuing written clause (読み, 変え, し, 来/き); noun/na-adjective + であり. Finish the sentence with a predicate.
points.teachingChoice: Retrieve known verb stems in the written genre. The final predicate normally carries the overall tense; context supplies the relationship between clauses. Do not force stem-linked report clauses into peer chat or claim a new official N2 inventory item.

points.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + ものの; na-adjective + なものの or であるものの; noun + であるものの. Past attributive predicates also work.
points.teachingChoice: First acknowledge an actual fact, then describe a remaining contrary state. First-lesson essay uses familiar が; this form is taught before its scored second-lesson noun cloze. The unusual copula alternatives are explicitly named instead of treating noun/na-adjective attachment as identical.
points.sourceCaution: Teacher source identifies a written/considered tone and commonly reflective or disappointed result. No mechanical replacement of all casual けど; no request or uncertain future invitation as the second clause in the taught examples.

points.form: Unexpected existing/completed result にもかかわらず
sources: https://jlptsensei.com/learn-japanese-grammar/にも関わらず-にもかかわらず-nimo-kakawarazu-meaning/
points.formation: Plain verb/i-adjective + にもかかわらず; noun + にもかかわらず or であるにもかかわらず; na-adjective + であるにもかかわらず.
points.teachingChoice: Describe an actual result contrary to expectation. Preserve も for despite; without も, にかかわらず expresses independence/regardless-of and is a different construction. Noun rain example is gratitude toward actual visitors, not a forecast.
points.sourceCaution: Formal does not mean incapable of conveying emotion: context can communicate gratitude or criticism. Contrast with regardless-of is explained before its deliberately form-focused distractor, not silently assessed as an untaught independent lesson.

editorialReview.sceneChoice: Two twelve-line scenes: friends edit a draft; Bao agrees a deadline with his host mother's neighbourhood newsletter. Written forms occur in draft quotations or a considered report, not in every friend-chat line.
editorialReview.tasks: Twenty tasks, with explicit form-practice labels and situational reply styles. Reading questions require information in the Japanese essay; no English translation of the essay reveals the answers.
editorialReview.wordChecks: All 44 newly selected spelling/reading pairs exist in the restricted cached JMdict extraction. Examples and meanings remain authored and not dictionary-certified.
editorialReview.fixesBeforeRender: Replaced newly introduced concessives in first-lesson reading with familiar が. Removed a recent-unit reference from the rain cloze because 地域 did not occur. Every reading gloss occurs in its own passage.
editorialReview.remaining: Native sentence/listening review; final N2 whole-level review after core unit 16.
